name: General trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about a broad mix of everyday knowledge that fits none of the other categories. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, which mineral is the softest, rated 1?
items.explain: The Mohs scale runs from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond), and talc is the softest of the ten reference minerals.

source.title: Mohs hardness | Britannica

items.question: Which mineral is the reference mineral for hardness 4 on the Mohs scale?
items.explain: The Mohs reference minerals in order are talc, gypsum, calcite, fluorite, apatite, feldspar, quartz, topaz, corundum and diamond, so fluorite is 4.

source.title: The Mohs Hardness Scale And Chart For Select Gems

items.question: Which mineral is the reference point for hardness 7 on the Mohs scale?
items.explain: Quartz is the Mohs reference mineral for 7, between feldspar (6) and topaz (8).

source.title: The Mohs Hardness Scale And Chart For Select Gems

items.question: In the traditional list of wedding anniversary gifts, which material marks the 15th anniversary?
items.explain: Traditional lists give crystal for the 15th year, with lace at 13, ivory at 14 and china at 20.

source.title: Traditional Wedding Anniversary Gifts

items.question: Which gemstone is traditionally associated with a 40th wedding anniversary?
items.explain: Traditional lists assign ruby to the 40th anniversary, after pearl (30th) and before sapphire (45th).

source.title: Traditional Wedding Anniversary Gifts

items.question: Which gemstone is the traditional gift for a 60th wedding anniversary?
items.explain: The traditional 60th anniversary gift is diamond, which is why the milestone is called the diamond anniversary.

source.title: Traditional Wedding Anniversary Gifts

items.question: Which gemstone is the standard birthstone for September?
items.explain: Sapphire is the standard birthstone for September; opal is October's, ruby is July's and emerald is May's.

source.title: Birthstones by Month: Chart and Photos

items.question: Which gemstone is the usual birthstone for February?
items.explain: Amethyst, a purple quartz, is the birthstone for February. Garnet is January's and aquamarine is March's.

source.title: Birthstones by Month: Chart and Photos

items.question: In which year did the US National Association of Jewelers meet in Kansas City and officially adopt a standard list of birthstones?
items.explain: The association adopted an official list in August 1912. Later updates, such as the 1952 additions, built on that list.

source.title: Birthstone - Wikipedia

items.question: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, which code word stands for the letter M?
items.explain: The 26 NATO code words run Alfa, Bravo, Charlie and so on, and the word for M is Mike.

source.title: Phonetic Alphabet

items.question: What is the NATO phonetic alphabet technically classed as, since it is not used to transcribe speech sounds?
items.explain: It gives clear code words for letters, so it is a spelling alphabet. It is not a phonetic transcription system like the International Phonetic Alphabet.

source.title: NATO phonetic alphabet - Wikipedia

items.question: In which year did the modified code words used in the NATO phonetic alphabet become the international standard, once ICAO accepted them?
items.explain: NATO modified the ICAO code words in 1956, and the set became the international standard when ICAO accepted it that year.

source.title: NATO phonetic alphabet - EPFL Graph Search

items.question: In the Dewey Decimal Classification, which hundreds range is devoted to Literature?
items.explain: The ten main classes include 400 Language, 700 Arts & recreation, 800 Literature and 900 History & geography.

source.title: Introduction to the Dewey Decimal Classification (OCLC)

items.question: In what year did Melvil Dewey develop the Dewey Decimal Classification library system?
items.explain: Melvil Dewey developed the system in 1876. It organizes library materials by subject using a hierarchical decimal numbering.

source.title: What Is the Dewey Decimal Classification System?

items.question: Who created the Olympic rings symbol?
items.explain: Pierre de Coubertin, founder of the modern Olympic movement, created the five interlaced rings symbol.

source.title: Olympic rings - Symbol of the Olympic Movement

items.question: According to the Olympic Charter, what do the five interlaced Olympic rings represent?
answers: The union of the five continents
items.correct: The union of the five continents
items.explain: The rings stand for the union of the five continents and the meeting of athletes from around the world at the Games.

source.title: Olympic rings - Symbol of the Olympic Movement

items.question: In what year were the Olympic rings first publicly presented?
items.explain: The rings were publicly presented for the first time in 1913, though they only debuted at a Games in 1920.

source.title: Olympic rings - Symbol of the Olympic Movement

items.question: At which city's Summer Olympics did the Olympic rings and flag officially debut in 1920?
items.explain: The symbol and flag officially debuted at the 1920 Summer Olympics in Antwerp, Belgium, after World War I delayed earlier plans.

source.title: Olympic symbols - Wikipedia

items.question: Which Royal Navy officer developed the wind force scale that runs from Force 0 (calm) to Force 12?
items.explain: Sir Francis Beaufort developed the scale in the early 1800s while in the Royal Navy.

source.title: NOAA Beaufort Wind Scale - Storm Prediction Center

items.question: What is Force 12, the top of the standard 0–12 Beaufort scale, called?
items.explain: Force 12 is hurricane-force wind. After that, the Saffir-Simpson scale ranks storms by category.

source.title: Beaufort Wind Scale: All 13 Forces from Calm to Hurricane, Explained

items.question: What did Beaufort's original wind scale describe, rather than a measured wind speed?
answers: The effect of the wind on a ship's sails
The reading on a ship's barometer
The height of the clouds overhead
The saltiness of the sea spray
items.correct: The effect of the wind on a ship's sails
items.explain: The original scale described the wind's effect on a ship's sails, not its speed. Speed equivalents were agreed later.

source.title: JetStream Max: Wind and Sea Scales - NOAA

items.question: Which ISO 216 paper size measures 210 × 297 mm?
items.explain: A4 is 210 × 297 mm and is the most commonly available paper size worldwide.

source.title: A Paper Sizes

items.question: The ISO A-series of paper sizes is built on a base sheet, A0, with what area?
items.explain: A0 is defined as one square metre, and each smaller size in the series is exactly half the area of the previous one.

source.title: Paper Drafting Sizes - ISO 216 series A, B and C

items.question: All ISO paper sizes share which width-to-length ratio?
items.explain: The ratio of 1 to the square root of 2 means a sheet folded in half keeps the same proportions.

source.title: Paper size - Wikipedia

items.question: The international ISO 216 paper size standard is based on which earlier national standard?
items.explain: ISO 216 is based on the German DIN 476 standard, which is why A4 is still called DIN A4 in Germany and Austria.

source.title: Paper size - Wikipedia

items.question: In which country was the Rubik's Cube invented?
items.explain: Ernő Rubik, a Hungarian sculptor and professor of architecture, invented the cube in 1974.

source.title: Rubik's Cube - Wikipedia

items.question: What was the Rubik's Cube originally called before it was renamed for worldwide sale?
items.explain: Rubik's puzzle was first called the Magic Cube (bűvös kocka in Hungarian). It was renamed Rubik's Cube for international release.

source.title: Rubik's Cube - Wikipedia

items.question: In what year did Ideal Toy begin selling the puzzle worldwide under the name Rubik's Cube?
items.explain: Ideal Toy renamed the puzzle and put it in stores in 1980, after Rubik invented it in 1974.

source.title: Rubik's Cube - The Strong National Museum of Play

items.question: What was Lizzie Magie's original aim in designing The Landlord's Game, the forerunner of Monopoly?
answers: To promote tourism in Atlantic City
To show the harm caused by land monopolies
To raise funds for Quaker charities
items.correct: To show the harm caused by land monopolies
items.explain: Magie wanted to publicize Henry George's reforms, which held that land monopolies were a root cause of inequality.

source.title: Playing Monopoly (and its discontents) on its 80th anniversary - Smithsonian

items.question: To which games company did Charles Darrow sell his rights to Monopoly in 1935?
items.explain: Darrow sold the rights to Parker Brothers in March 1935, and the company began selling the game almost immediately.

source.title: Playing Monopoly (and its discontents) on its 80th anniversary - Smithsonian

items.question: What was the name of the board game Lizzie Magie patented in 1904 that later inspired Monopoly?
items.explain: Magie's patented game, The Landlord's Game, was the basis for the version Charles Darrow later sold as Monopoly.

source.title: The Game of Monopoly is Patented - Library of Congress

items.question: In what year did Louis Braille develop his six-dot reading system for blind people?
items.explain: Braille developed his six-dot cell in 1824 as a teenager at the school for the blind in Paris.

source.title: Braille | Britannica

items.question: How many different characters can the six-dot Braille cell form, not counting a blank cell?
items.explain: Each of the six dots is raised or not, giving 63 patterns once the all-blank cell is excluded.

source.title: Braille | Britannica

items.question: Braille's system grew out of a twelve-dot military code for reading in the dark. What was that code called?
items.explain: Soldiers used the twelve-dot night writing code to communicate after dark, and Braille simplified it to a six-dot cell.

source.title: Description and History of Braille - American Council of the Blind

items.question: At what age was Louis Braille blinded?
items.explain: Braille lost his sight in an accident at the age of three and went on to invent the tactile system that bears his name.

source.title: Braille | Britannica

items.question: Which of these century years was NOT a leap year in the Gregorian calendar?
items.explain: Century years must be divisible by 400 to be leap years, so 1900 was not one, while 1600, 2000 and 2400 are.

source.title: Leap Years - U.S. Naval Observatory

items.question: How many leap years occur in each 400-year cycle of the Gregorian calendar?
items.explain: The Gregorian rule introduces 97 leap days every 400 years, not the 100 a simple every-fourth-year rule would give.

source.title: Leap Years - U.S. Naval Observatory

items.question: What is the average length of a year in the Gregorian calendar?
items.explain: Because 97 leap days fall in every 400 years, the average Gregorian year is 365.2425 days, close to the tropical year.

source.title: Leap Years - U.S. Naval Observatory

items.question: A marathon is 26 miles plus how many yards?
items.explain: The standard marathon is 26 miles 385 yards (42.195 km), a distance that comes from the 1908 London Olympic course.

source.title: Athletics at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon - Wikipedia

items.question: The modern standard marathon distance traces back to the Olympic Games held in which city and year?
items.explain: The 1908 London Olympic marathon was the first run over 26 miles 385 yards, which became the standard distance.

source.title: Athletics at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon - Wikipedia

items.question: The 1908 Olympic marathon started at which royal residence?
items.explain: The British Olympic Committee started the 1908 race at Windsor Castle and finished it in front of the royal box at the stadium in London.

source.title: Marathon | Britannica

items.question: According to legend, the Greek soldier who ran from Marathon to Athens in 490 BCE brought news of victory over whom?
items.explain: The legend says the soldier ran to announce the Athenian victory over the Persians, and the marathon race commemorates it.

source.title: Marathon | Britannica

items.question: In which year was the marathon added to the women's Olympic program?
items.explain: Women's marathon running joined the Olympic program in 1984. The men's race dates from the first modern Games in 1896.

source.title: Marathon | Britannica

items.question: What does the Scoville scale measure the concentration of?
items.explain: Scoville heat units measure capsaicin and related capsaicinoids, the compounds that make chili peppers hot.

source.title: The Scoville Scale: Complete Pepper Heat Chart - Chili Pepper Madness

items.question: Which of these chili peppers typically rates hottest on the Scoville scale?
items.explain: Habaneros typically score 100,000–350,000 SHU. Serranos reach about 10,000–25,000, and jalapeños and guajillos about 2,500–10,000.

source.title: Scoville scale - Wikipedia

items.question: Which American inventor patented an early typewriter in 1868 and is credited with the QWERTY layout?
items.explain: Christopher Latham Sholes invented the typewriter whose keyboard evolved into QWERTY, and E. Remington and Sons later popularized it.

source.title: Where Did the QWERTY Keyboard Layout Come From?

items.question: How did the QWERTY keyboard layout get its name?
answers: From the first six letters on the top letter row
From a Latin word for typing
From the first letters of the alphabet reversed
items.correct: From the first six letters on the top letter row
items.explain: QWERTY is named after the first six letter keys at the top left of a standard English-language keyboard.

source.title: QWERTY Keyboard Meaning, History & Layout - Study.com

items.question: Which alternative keyboard layout, designed in the 1930s, was meant to be faster and more comfortable than QWERTY?
items.explain: The Dvorak layout, designed in the 1930s, was meant to be more efficient than QWERTY, but QWERTY stayed the global standard.

source.title: Where Did the QWERTY Keyboard Layout Come From?

items.question: Which variant of the QWERTY layout is used in German-speaking countries?
items.explain: German-speaking countries adjust the layout to QWERTZ, which swaps the positions of Y and Z.

source.title: QWERTY Keyboard Meaning, History & Layout - Study.com
